verdict.rationale: Activepieces documents its own AI agents with tool use. You attach specific app actions, the agent can search 760+ apps, and flows can be handed to an agent as tools. Bring-your-own AI keys suggests some provider choice. However, the evidence presents agents as standalone workers that call flows, not as steps placed inside a workflow. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an AI agent or LLM step inside a flow, explicit per-step model selection, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can add AI agent or LLM steps inside a workflow, with model choice and tool use

citations.quote: You attach individual actions, not whole apps. An agent given Send message can post to Slack and nothing else.
It searches Slack, Linear, Drive, or any of 760+ apps at the moment it needs the answer
When part of a job has to happen the same way every time, build that part as a flow and hand it over.
You set the goal and choose which apps, flows and files the agent can use. It decides the steps and carries them out.
